rules: Require evidence for readiness; do not treat a planned check as a passed check.
Name owners, dependencies, rollout stages, and rollback authority.
Separate blockers, waivers, and follow-up work.
acceptance_checks: Every item has an observable completion signal.
A failed gate leads to a named safe action.

rules: Organize procedures around signals and decisions, not a flat command list.
Cover diagnosis, mitigation, rollback, escalation, and evidence capture.
Mark unsupported operational details unresolved rather than inventing them.
acceptance_checks: A responder can choose the next step from observed evidence.
No unverified command is presented as safe to execute.

rules: Separate facts from hypotheses and avoid blame.
Trace contributing conditions across process, system, and response.
Make corrective actions specific, owned, prioritized, and verifiable.
acceptance_checks: The analysis explains why defenses failed, not only what broke.
Each action has a completion test.
